entries.title: Daniel 1:1
segments: In the third year; see note on

entries.title: Daniel 1:2
segments: Gave Jekoiakim--into his hand; he became the servant of Nebuchadnezzar, but continued to reign in Jerusalem, for his reign lasted eleven years,

.  After reigning three years, he revolted against Nebuchadnezzar, and the remaining years of his reign were rendered miserable by the invasion of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites.  From
, it seems probable that his reign was terminated by a second invasion of Nebuchadnezzar, who carried him captive to Babylon.

entries.title: Daniel 1:3
segments:
Master of his eunuchs; a great number of eunuchs are employed now, as anciently, in eastern courts; they have, charge of the monarch's household, and all its arrangements. 
 
vv 3-5. 
 
When God punishes nations for their sins, he is able to protect and provide for his faithful servants; and times of great public calamity often become to them occasions of high perferment and usefulness.

entries.title: Daniel 1:4
segments:
Children in whom was no blemish; in eastern courts, it is the custom now, as of old, to select the fairest and most noble among the captive youth to wait upon the monarch.  These are carefully trained up under the chief of the eunuchs, but are not themselves made eunuchs. 
 
  Ability; strength of body and mind.

entries.title: Daniel 1:5
segments: A daily provision; for the purpose of making them full fleshed, and of good appearance.  See note on

entries.title: Daniel 1:7
segments: Gave names; new names; a practice still retained in oriental courts.

entries.title: Daniel 1:8
segments:
Defile himself; the food and drink prepared by the heathen he regarded as unclean, according to the distinctions of the Mosaic law. It is probable that he wished also to avoid a luxurious and effeminate style of living ill becoming the servants of Jehovah. 
 
  The king's meat; literally, "the king's dainties." 
 
The true believer will value purity of heart and life, and visible conformity to God's law, above all earthly delights and honors.

entries.title: Daniel 1:12
segments:
Pulse; the word in the original seems to denote any vegetable food. 
 
vv 12-16. 
 
It is by temperance and simplicity in food and drink, and not by luxury, that both body and mind are preserved in the highest health and vigor.

entries.title: Daniel 1:20
segments: They who choose their attendance from those who have been trained in the knowledge and fear of God, will be best served.

entries.title: Daniel 1:21
segments: Unto the first year of king Cyrus; that is, he lived to see the termination of the Babylonian empire.  The words must not be understood to mean that he did not continue longer.  Compare
